title: Paloma and the Letter
premise: In 1847, apprentice clockmaker Emrys Fairweather is summoned to a river-town observatory to repair its failing master clock, where he discovers that the observatory's dying keeper, Paloma, has hidden a letter inside the clock's case—a confession implicating the town's founding families in a massacre they rewrote as heroism. When the season's first ice closes the only bridge, Emrys is trapped with the guilty heirs who have come to destroy the letter before the river thaws and the outside world's historians arrive. As the heirs turn on each other and Paloma's health fails, Emrys must transcribe and smuggle the truth out, ending with the letter published as the ice breaks—Paloma dead but vindicated, and Emrys choosing to sign his name to an account that will cost him the town that raised him.
about_author: Sebastian Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging municipal records in river towns along the northern trade routes, where he first encountered the gaps left by victors' histories. He writes historical fiction that asks what ordinary witnesses owe to the record, and lives within earshot of a working clock tower.

chapters.title: The Clock That Kept Two Times
chapters.summary: Emrys arrives at the observatory to repair the master clock, which is running two minutes fast for no mechanical reason he can find. The ailing keeper, Paloma, watches him work in pointed silence. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: wary curiosity—the first hint that the clock's error is deliberate.

chapters.title: What the Case Held
chapters.summary: Disassembling the movement, Emrys finds a sealed letter wedged behind the striking train. Paloma admits she wrote it and asks him to read it only if he can promise to deliver it. He cannot yet promise. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the shock of discovery and the weight of an unfinished oath.

chapters.title: The Heirs Arrive
chapters.summary: The bridge closes with the first ice, stranding the town. That evening, three heirs of the founding families arrive uninvited, claiming they've come to honor the dying keeper. Emrys recognizes their names from the letter. POV: Emrys, with a brief Paloma interlude. Emotional beat: dread disguised as courtesy.

chapters.title: Paloma's Account
chapters.summary: Paloma, feverish, tells Emrys the full story: the massacre at the mill, the letter her father was forced to sign, the history the families paid to have written. She explains the clock's two-minute error—it strikes the true time of the massacre each midnight. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Emrys searches his twelve years of apprenticeship for a way to hide the letter, recalling every silence that once protected him. The eldest heir, Aldous, begins quietly questioning the household staff, buying loyalty. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the cost of caution—his survival instincts are exactly what the heirs are counting on.

chapters.title: A Search by Lamplight
chapters.summary: The heirs ransack the observatory while Emrys is sent on an errand across the frozen river; they find the clock case empty—he has already moved the letter. Suspicion falls on the household. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guilt, as his cleverness endangers the innocent people around him.

chapters.title: The Midnight Strike
chapters.summary: At midnight the repaired clock strikes the massacre's true hour, and the heirs realize Paloma built the confession into the mechanism itself—every clockmaker in the valley could read it. Aldous decides Paloma cannot be allowed to recover. POV: Aldous, then Emrys. Emotional beat: the corruption of inheritance into desperation.

chapters.title: What the Ice Takes
chapters.summary: Paloma collapses; the household doctor, bought by the heirs, withholds treatment. Emrys copies the letter by candlelight and entrusts the original to the one person the heirs cannot intimidate: the ferryman's daughter, who knows the river paths. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full view.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Aldous confronts Emrys with an offer—apprenticeship to the family firm, a lifetime of comfort—for the copy. Emrys stalls, then publicly winds the master clock before the assembled town, forcing the heirs to hear the true hour strike in front of witnesses. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: climax—the silence finally broken on the record.

chapters.title: The Letter, Signed
chapters.summary: The ice breaks; the ferryman's daughter's copy reaches the district historian. Paloma dies at dawn with the clock striking true, and Emrys signs his name to the published account, knowing the town will never forgive him. He leaves across the open bridge. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: sorrowful resolution—truth preserved, home forfeited, inheritance redefined.
